stem: Which of the following describes a 'Koala Hold' position of comfort?

options.text: The child sits on the parent's lap facing them, with arms and legs wrapped around the parent.
The child is swaddled tightly in a blanket and placed on an examination table.
The parent stands behind the child while the child sits on the edge of the bed.
The child lies on their side while the parent holds their legs still.

explanation: This position provides secure skin-to-skin contact and makes the child feel safe and upright rather than helpless.
rationale: Imagine the way the animal this hold is named after clings to its mother.

optionExplanations.A: This position provides secure skin-to-skin contact and makes the child feel safe and upright rather than helpless.
optionExplanations.B: This describes a wrapping technique for babies, but it does not involve the specific 'clinging' posture of a koala hold.
optionExplanations.C: This is a supportive position, but it lacks the chest-to-chest contact characteristic of the koala hold.
optionExplanations.D: Lying down often increases a child's feeling of helplessness; the koala hold is an upright position.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: The child sits on the parent's lap facing them, with arms and legs wrapped around the parent.
